title: BBQ Chicken Mac n Cheese

ingredients.item: salt and freshly cracked black pepper
salt and black pepper (pasta water and sauce)

steps: Start the pasta water first (see Mac n cheese) so it's boiling by the time the chicken is done.
Slice the chicken lengthways into thin, even strips, then cut across into small-to-medium pieces so they all cook at the same rate.
In a large bowl, toss the chicken with the onion powder, garlic powder, smoked paprika, thyme, oregano, chili flakes, 2 tsp of the oil, a pinch of salt and plenty of black pepper until evenly coated.

Heat a large pan over high heat until very hot. Add the remaining 2 tsp oil and the chicken, scraping in all the spices, and spread it into one layer. Work in batches if the pan is crowded so the chicken sears instead of stewing.

Leave it untouched for 2 minutes to form a crust, then stir only occasionally until just cooked through, about 4½ minutes in total. Stir in the BBQ sauce and cook 1 minute more to glaze. Tip the chicken into a bowl.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil over high heat. Salt it, add the macaroni and stir so it doesn't clump. Cook for 1 minute less than the packet says, then drain.
Grate the cheddar on the large holes of a box grater.

Put the chicken pan back over medium-high heat without wiping it. Add the cream or milk, cream cheese, cheddar, a pinch of salt and some pepper, and stir to break up the cream cheese and melt everything. Add the optional spices now if using.
Once it simmers, drop the heat to medium so it doesn't over-reduce, and cook 2–3 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Add the drained pasta and stir over medium heat until every piece is coated.
Fold the BBQ chicken through for about 30 seconds, until evenly mixed. (Or keep the chicken and mac separate.)
Divide between 6 containers and garnish with parmesan, chopped parsley and black pepper.

To store, cool for 15–20 minutes before putting the lids on. Keeps 3–4 days in the fridge or about 3 months frozen; thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge. Reheat in the microwave or a pan with a splash of water or stock.
notes: 2026-10-11 — Tasty enough to eat it, boring enough for me to not overeat it
